title: Develop an Idea Desarrollar una Idea

blocks.en: Unit Two · Stage 1: Build the Foundation
blocks.es_reference: Unidad Dos · Etapa 1: Construir el Fundamento

blocks.en: Develop an Idea
blocks.es_reference: Desarrollar una Idea

blocks.en: Idea, probing question, keyword, subject, objective — the five tools that turn a text into a sermon.
blocks.es_reference: Idea, pregunta de sondeo, palabra clave, sujeto, objetivo — las cinco herramientas que convierten un texto en sermón.

blocks.en: 2.1 The Idea
blocks.es_reference: 2.1 La Idea

blocks.en: After you have a text, the next foundational material is the idea. The idea is the general topic of the sermon, and it must come from the Scripture itself. Donald Miller laid down a rule that has shaped a generation of preachers: the theme of the text and the theme of the sermon must be the same. If they are not, the text is no longer a text — it is a pretext, a starting point for the preacher's own thoughts. The idea answers the question, "What is the general topic of this text?"
blocks.es_reference: Después de tener un texto, el siguiente material fundamental es la idea. La idea es el tema general del sermón, y debe surgir de la Escritura misma. Donald Miller estableció una regla que ha moldeado a una generación de predicadores: el tema del texto y el tema del sermón deben ser el mismo. Si no lo son, el texto deja de ser texto y se vuelve un pretexto, un punto de partida para los propios pensamientos del predicador. La idea responde a la pregunta: «¿Cuál es el tema general de este texto?»

blocks.en: Examples of an idea include: faith, the kingdom of God, hope, law, grieving the Holy Spirit, works, love, fasting, baptism, singleness, growing, family. Each of these is a real Biblical idea — but each is also far too general to preach in one sermon. Try preaching on faith. You could speak about the qualities of faith, the demands of faith, examples of faith, men of faith, or reasons faith is important — and each of these would itself be a full sermon. The idea is the raw quarry stone. It must be cut down before it can be set in a wall.
blocks.es_reference: Ejemplos de una idea incluyen: la fe, el reino de Dios, la esperanza, la ley, el contristar al Espíritu Santo, las obras, el amor, el ayuno, el bautismo, la soltería, el crecer, la familia. Cada una de estas es una idea bíblica real, pero cada una es también demasiado general para predicarse en un solo sermón. Intente predicar sobre la fe. Podría hablar de las cualidades de la fe, las exigencias de la fe, ejemplos de fe, hombres de fe, o razones por las que la fe es importante, y cada uno de estos sería en sí mismo un sermón completo. La idea es la piedra en bruto de la cantera. Debe ser cortada antes de poder colocarse en un muro.

blocks.en: The tool that cuts the idea down is the probing question. But before you reach for that tool, you have to have the stone. Open your text and ask the simple question: "What is this passage about?" Whatever single noun or phrase comes back is your idea. Resist the temptation to make it clever. The idea should be plain. Cleverness comes later.
blocks.es_reference: Después que tenga un texto, el siguiente material fundamental es la idea. La idea es el tema general del sermón, y debe venir de la Escritura misma. Donald Miller estableció una regla: el tema del texto y el tema del sermón deben ser el mismo. Si no lo son, el texto ya no es un texto — es un pretexto. Ejemplos de una idea: fe, el reino de Dios, esperanza, ley, amor, ayuno, bautismo, crecimiento, familia. Cada una es demasiado general para predicar en un solo sermón. La idea es la piedra de cantera en bruto; debe cortarse antes de colocarse en un muro.

blocks.en: 2.2 The Probing Question
blocks.es_reference: 2.2 La Pregunta de Sondeo

blocks.en: The probing question is the tool that narrows the idea to a manageable size. The news industry uses these same questions to produce a story. Rudyard Kipling wrote a poem in The Elephant's Child that is the easiest way to remember them:
blocks.es_reference: La pregunta de sondeo es la herramienta que reduce la idea a un tamaño manejable. La industria de las noticias usa estas mismas preguntas para producir una nota. Rudyard Kipling escribió un poema en The Elephant’s Child que es la manera más fácil de recordarlas:

blocks.en:
Kipling's Six Honest Servants
I keep six honest serving men
They taught me all I knew,
Their names are What and Why and When
And How and Where and Who.
blocks.es_reference:
Los Seis Sirvientes de Kipling
Mantengo a seis sirvientes honestos
Me enseñaron todo lo que sabía.
Sus nombres son Qué, Por qué, Cuándo,
Cómo, Dónde y Quién.

blocks.en: For preaching purposes, Kipling's six become eight by adding which and how much. So the eight interrogatives are: who, which, what, why, when, where, how, and how much. The probing question is formed by putting the idea together with one of these interrogatives in a complete sentence question.
blocks.es_reference: Para los propósitos de la predicación, las seis de Kipling se vuelven ocho al añadir cuál y cuánto. Así, los ocho interrogativos son: quién, cuál, qué, por qué, cuándo, dónde, cómo y cuánto. La pregunta de sondeo se forma al unir la idea con uno de estos interrogativos en una pregunta de oración completa.

blocks.en: Take the idea of hope. Each interrogative produces a different probing question, and each probing question will produce a different sermon:
blocks.es_reference: Tome la idea de la esperanza. Cada interrogativo produce una pregunta de sondeo distinta, y cada pregunta de sondeo producirá un sermón distinto:

blocks.en:
Who generally points to people. "Who has hope?"
Which points to types or kinds. "Which kinds of hope are valid?"
What points to steps, ways, or qualities. "What are the values of hope?"
Why points to reasons. "Why is hope necessary?"
When points to times. "When do we need hope?"
Where points to places. "Where do we find hope?"
How points to procedures or ways. "How is hope obtained, or lost?"
How much points to quantity. "How much hope do we need?"
blocks.es_reference:
Quién generalmente apunta a personas. «¿Quién tiene esperanza?»
Cuál apunta a tipos o clases. «¿Cuáles clases de esperanza son válidas?»
Qué apunta a pasos, maneras o cualidades. «¿Cuáles son los valores de la esperanza?»
Por qué apunta a razones. «¿Por qué es necesaria la esperanza?»
Cuándo apunta a tiempos. «¿Cuándo necesitamos esperanza?»
Dónde apunta a lugares. «¿Dónde hallamos esperanza?»
Cómo apunta a procedimientos o maneras. «¿Cómo se obtiene, o se pierde, la esperanza?»
Cuánto apunta a cantidad. «¿Cuánta esperanza necesitamos?»

blocks.en: Notice that the same idea — hope — has just produced eight different sermons. Each is legitimate. Each is Biblical. Each will require a different sermon outline. The probing question has done the cutting work that the idea alone could not do.
blocks.es_reference: La pregunta de sondeo es la herramienta que reduce la idea a un tamaño manejable. Los ocho interrogativos son: quién, cuál, qué, por qué, cuándo, dónde, cómo y cuánto. Tome la idea de esperanza. Cada interrogativo produce una pregunta de sondeo diferente, y cada pregunta producirá un sermón diferente: "¿Quién tiene esperanza?", "¿Cuáles tipos de esperanza son válidos?", "¿Cuáles son los valores de la esperanza?", "¿Por qué es necesaria la esperanza?", "¿Cuándo necesitamos esperanza?", "¿Dónde encontramos esperanza?", "¿Cómo se obtiene la esperanza?", "¿Cuánta esperanza necesitamos?" La misma idea acaba de producir ocho sermones diferentes.

blocks.en: 2.3 The Keyword
blocks.es_reference: 2.3 La Palabra Clave

blocks.en: The keyword arises naturally from the probing question. It is usually a plural noun, and it is the single most important word in your sermon's structure — because the keyword is what unites the outline. Every point of the sermon will be a particular instance of the keyword.
blocks.es_reference: La palabra clave surge naturalmente de la pregunta de sondeo. Suele ser un sustantivo plural, y es la palabra más importante en la estructura de su sermón, porque la palabra clave es lo que une el bosquejo. Cada punto del sermón será un caso particular de la palabra clave.

blocks.en: Three rules govern the keyword. First, it is always plural. Almost without exception, your keyword will end in -s. Check yours: if it does not end in -s and is not an irregular plural like "people" or "men," it is probably wrong. Second, only one keyword per sermon. Just as you must use only one interrogative, you must use only one keyword. Third, avoid generic words like "things." "Three things about prayer" is not a keyword; it is laziness. The keyword should be as specific as possible to the actual content of your divisions.
blocks.es_reference: Tres reglas gobiernan la palabra clave. Primera: siempre es plural. Casi sin excepción, su palabra clave terminará en -s. Verifique la suya: si no termina en -s y no es un plural irregular, probablemente está equivocada. Segunda: solo una palabra clave por sermón. Así como debe usar un solo interrogativo, debe usar una sola palabra clave. Tercera: evite palabras genéricas como «cosas». «Tres cosas sobre la oración» no es una palabra clave; es pereza. La palabra clave debe ser tan específica como sea posible respecto al contenido real de sus divisiones.

blocks.en: Watch how the keyword arises from each probing question on the idea of faith:
blocks.es_reference: Observe cómo la palabra clave surge de cada pregunta de sondeo sobre la idea de la fe:

blocks.en:
Who are some people of great faith? Keyword = people.
Which are the elements of faith? Keyword = elements.
What are the ingredients of faith? Keyword = ingredients.
What are the effects of faith? Keyword = effects. (Possible outline: seeing the invisible, doing the impossible, believing the incredible.)
Why have faith? Keyword = reasons. (Possible outline: abundant life, eternal life.)
When should we have faith? Keyword = times. (When discouraged, when distracted, when disappointed.)
Where may faith be found? Keyword = places. (Before the throne, in the closet, near the cross.)
How do we show faith? Keyword = ways. (By word, by walk, by witness.)
How much faith do we need? Keyword = amounts. (Enough to cover sorrow, enough to fill our lives, enough to overflow into joy.)
blocks.es_reference:
¿Quiénes son algunas personas de gran fe? Palabra clave = personas.
¿Cuáles son los elementos de la fe? Palabra clave = elementos.
¿Cuáles son los ingredientes de la fe? Palabra clave = ingredientes.
¿Cuáles son los efectos de la fe? Palabra clave = efectos. (Bosquejo posible: ver lo invisible, hacer lo imposible, creer lo increíble.)
¿Por qué tener fe? Palabra clave = razones. (Bosquejo posible: vida abundante, vida eterna.)
¿Cuándo debemos tener fe? Palabra clave = tiempos. (Cuando estamos desanimados, distraídos, decepcionados.)
¿Dónde puede hallarse la fe? Palabra clave = lugares. (Ante el trono, en el aposento, junto a la cruz.)
¿Cómo mostramos la fe? Palabra clave = maneras. (Por palabra, por andar, por testimonio.)
¿Cuánta fe necesitamos? Palabra clave = cantidades. (Suficiente para cubrir la tristeza, suficiente para llenar nuestras vidas, suficiente para desbordar en gozo.)

blocks.en: A list of keywords useful in preaching: actions, advantages, affirmations, aims, alternatives, answers, applications, areas, attitudes, attributes, barriers, beliefs, benefits, blessings, changes, comparisons, conditions, contrasts, dangers, demands, duties, elements, examples, expressions, facts, failures, fears, fundamentals, gifts, groups, ideas, ingredients, insights, instances, instruments, joys, justifications, kinds, lessons, losses, methods, needs, occasions, opinions, opportunities, principles, problems, proofs, promises, provisions, questions, qualities, reactions, reasons, results, rewards, rules, secrets, sins, stages, steps, successes, testimonies, tests, topics, trials, truths, types, targets, uses, values, views, warnings, ways, words.
blocks.es_reference: La palabra clave surge naturalmente de la pregunta de sondeo. Es generalmente un sustantivo plural, y es la palabra más importante en la estructura de su sermón — porque la palabra clave une el bosquejo. Tres reglas: siempre es plural (terminando casi siempre en -s); solo una palabra clave por sermón; evite palabras genéricas como "cosas". Algunas palabras clave útiles: razones, maneras, tiempos, lugares, elementos, ingredientes, pasos, principios, lecciones, ejemplos, problemas, promesas, peligros, beneficios, advertencias.

blocks.en: 2.4 The Subject
blocks.es_reference: 2.4 El Sujeto

blocks.en: Having a clear subject is what prevents aimless wandering in preaching. I remember walking through the woods with my father as a boy. I would have been hopelessly lost — every tree looked the same — but my father pulled out his compass at intervals. The compass gave him a fixed point of reference; we did not wander. The subject of a sermon is its compass.
blocks.es_reference: Tener un sujeto claro es lo que evita el divagar sin rumbo en la predicación. Recuerdo caminar por el bosque con mi padre cuando era niño. Yo me habría perdido sin remedio, pues cada árbol parecía igual, pero mi padre sacaba su brújula a intervalos. La brújula le daba un punto fijo de referencia; no divagábamos. El sujeto de un sermón es su brújula.

blocks.en: The subject is the keyword plus a modifier. A modifier is anything that describes or limits the keyword. Three forms of modifier are common. The first is the adjective: "seven deadly sins" — the words "seven" and "deadly" both modify the keyword "sins." The second is the prepositional phrase: "ways of gaining faith" — the keyword is "ways," and "of gaining faith" is a prepositional phrase that modifies it. The third is the subordinate clause: "qualities that God possesses" — "qualities" is the keyword, and "that God possesses" is a clause that modifies it.
blocks.es_reference: El sujeto es la palabra clave más un modificador. Un modificador es cualquier cosa que describa o limite la palabra clave. Tres formas de modificador son comunes. La primera es el adjetivo: «siete pecados mortales», donde las palabras «siete» y «mortales» modifican la palabra clave «pecados». La segunda es la frase preposicional: «maneras de ganar fe», donde la palabra clave es «maneras», y «de ganar fe» es una frase preposicional que la modifica. La tercera es la cláusula subordinada: «cualidades que Dios posee», donde «cualidades» es la palabra clave, y «que Dios posee» es una cláusula que la modifica.

blocks.en: The subject answers the question, "What is the sermon about?" If you ask the probing question, "What are some ways of gaining faith?", the keyword is "ways" and the subject is "ways of gaining faith." Each division of the outline will be one specific way of gaining faith. The congregation, when they take notes, will be able to write the subject at the top of their page and write each numbered point underneath. They will know what the sermon is about, and so will you.
blocks.es_reference: Tener un sujeto claro es lo que previene el deambular sin rumbo en la predicación. El sujeto es la palabra clave más un modificador. Tres formas: adjetivo ("siete pecados capitales"), frase preposicional ("maneras de obtener fe"), o cláusula subordinada ("cualidades que Dios posee"). El sujeto responde a la pregunta: "¿De qué trata el sermón?"

blocks.en: 2.5 The Objective
blocks.es_reference: 2.5 El Objetivo

blocks.en: The objective is the goal of the sermon. It answers the question, "What do I want people to do?" The objective should be phrased as an action, not as a belief or attitude — because beliefs and attitudes will follow when actions are right, but actions will not always follow when beliefs and attitudes are merely informed.
blocks.es_reference: El objetivo es la meta del sermón. Responde a la pregunta: «¿Qué quiero que la gente haga?» El objetivo debe expresarse como una acción, no como una creencia o actitud, porque las creencias y actitudes seguirán cuando las acciones sean correctas, pero las acciones no siempre seguirán cuando las creencias y actitudes están meramente informadas.

blocks.en: A useful formula is to begin the objective with the words "people will…" If your action is salvation, the objective might be: "People will respond during the invitation to receive Christ as Savior." If your subject deals with anger, the objective might be: "People will begin to control their anger during difficult situations." If your subject deals with prayer, the objective might be: "People will set aside a specific time each day for prayer this week." Each of these is concrete, each is measurable, and each gives the conclusion of your sermon a clear destination.
blocks.es_reference: Una fórmula útil es comenzar el objetivo con las palabras «la gente…». Si su acción es la salvación, el objetivo podría ser: «La gente responderá durante la invitación para recibir a Cristo como Salvador». Si su tema trata del enojo, el objetivo podría ser: «La gente comenzará a controlar su enojo durante situaciones difíciles». Si su tema trata de la oración, el objetivo podría ser: «La gente apartará un tiempo específico cada día para la oración esta semana». Cada uno de estos es concreto, cada uno es medible, y cada uno le da a la conclusión de su sermón un destino claro.

blocks.en: When you have completed the five tools of Unit 2 — idea, probing question, keyword, subject, and objective — you have completed the foundation. From Unit 3 forward you will use these foundational materials to construct outlines.
blocks.es_reference: El objetivo es la meta del sermón. Responde a la pregunta: "¿Qué quiero que la gente haga?" El objetivo debe formularse como una acción, no como una creencia o actitud. Una fórmula útil es comenzar con "la gente va a…" — "La gente responderá a la invitación para recibir a Cristo como Salvador"; "La gente comenzará a controlar su ira"; "La gente apartará un tiempo específico cada día para orar."

blocks.en: "Give diligence to present thyself approved unto God, a workman that needeth not to be ashamed, handling aright the word of truth."<cite>2 Timothy 2:15 (ASV)</cite>
blocks.es_reference: "Procura con diligencia presentarte á Dios aprobado, como obrero que no tiene de qué avergonzarse, que traza bien la palabra de verdad."<cite>2 Timoteo 2:15 (RV1909)</cite>

fill.prompt: If the theme of the text and the theme of the sermon are not the same, the text is no longer a text but a ____, a starting point for the preacher's own thoughts.
The idea is the raw ____ stone: it must be cut down before it can be set in a wall.
The ____ question is the tool that narrows the idea to a manageable size.
For preaching purposes, Kipling's six interrogatives become eight by adding which and ____.
Of the interrogatives, why points to ____, as in "Why is hope necessary?"
The first rule of the keyword is that it is always ____; almost without exception it ends in -s.
The third rule of the keyword forbids generic words such as ____, which the lesson calls laziness.
Like the tool the author's father used in the woods, the subject is the sermon's ____, a fixed point of reference that keeps it from wandering.
The subject is the keyword plus a ____, anything that describes or limits the keyword.
The objective answers "What do I want people to do?" and should be phrased as ____, not as a belief or attitude.

sa.prompt: Take the idea 'forgiveness' and develop all eight probing questions from it. For each, identify the likely keyword.
sa.model: Should produce 8 questions (who/which/what/why/when/where/how/how much) about forgiveness, with a plural keyword for each (people, kinds, qualities/effects, reasons, times, places, ways, amounts).

sa.prompt: A student presents this work: Idea = grace, Probing question = 'Why is grace amazing?', Keyword = 'amazing.' Identify two errors and fix them.
sa.model: Errors: (1) 'amazing' is an adjective, not a plural noun; (2) it does not arise naturally from 'why' — 'why' usually generates 'reasons.' Better: keyword 'reasons' and subject 'reasons grace is amazing.'

sa.prompt: Build a complete unified plan (idea, probing question, keyword, subject, objective) for a sermon on prayer aimed at a discouraged congregation.
sa.model: Should show all five elements coherent with each other. Idea = prayer. Probing question well-formed. Keyword plural. Subject = keyword + modifier. Objective phrased as action ('People will…').

sa.prompt: Explain in your own words why the keyword must be plural. Use the analogy of the outline as a row of shelves on which the points are stored.
sa.model: Should explain that the keyword names a category, and each point of the outline is a member of that category. A singular keyword cannot host multiple parallel points; only a plural can.

sa.prompt: Why does the course warn against using 'things' as a keyword? What does this warning teach about specificity in preaching?
sa.model: 'Things' is generic and tells the listener almost nothing. The warning teaches that vague keywords produce vague sermons; specific keywords (reasons, ways, dangers, examples) commit the preacher to a definite shape and the listener to a definite map.

sa.prompt: Construct three different subjects all using the keyword 'ways' but with three different modifiers (adjective, prepositional phrase, subordinate clause).
sa.model: Examples: adjective: 'effective ways'; prepositional phrase: 'ways of gaining faith'; subordinate clause: 'ways that God speaks.' Each is a legitimate subject built from the same keyword.

sa.prompt: Critique this objective: 'People will understand that God is sovereign.' Rewrite it as a proper objective.
sa.model: 'Understand' is a belief/attitude, not an action. Better: 'People will choose to trust God's plan even when they cannot see the outcome,' or 'People will name one situation this week where they will surrender control to God.'

sa.prompt: Compare the eight probing questions for the idea 'love.' Which would you choose to preach on Mother's Day, and which on Good Friday? Justify your choices.
sa.model: Mother's Day might use 'How does love show itself?' (ways) or 'What are the qualities of love?' (1 Cor 13). Good Friday might use 'What is the cost of love?' (effects/proofs) or 'Where do we see God's love most clearly?' (places — the Cross). Strong answer ties the choice to occasion.

sa.prompt: Take the idea 'patience' and build a complete unified plan: state the idea, form one probing question using a single interrogative, derive a plural keyword, write a subject (keyword + modifier), and phrase an action objective beginning 'People will…'.
sa.model: Strong answer shows all five elements coherent: idea = patience; one interrogative only; a plural keyword (e.g., reasons, ways, times); subject = keyword + modifier ('ways patience grows'); objective as a concrete action beginning 'People will…'. The keyword must be plural and the objective an action, not a belief.

sa.prompt: A student's objective reads: 'People will know that prayer is important.' Explain why this objective is weak, and rewrite it as a strong, measurable action objective.
sa.model: Strong answer identifies that 'know' names a belief, not an action, so it cannot be measured or implemented. A rewrite phrases a concrete action: e.g., 'People will set aside a specific time each day this week for prayer.' Good answers note that actions carry beliefs with them, but informed beliefs do not always produce action.
